key_insight: Fe or Cr substitution at Ni grain-boundary planes increases cohesion, with strengthening governed by element type and local atomic structure.
engineering_relevance: Atomistically predicted separation energies and peak tractions can inform continuum fracture models for multicomponent Ni-based alloys.
method: Compute DFT rigid-body separation curves for six symmetric-tilt Ni grain boundaries.
Extract work of separation and maximum traction using the universal binding energy relation.
Benchmark ML interatomic potentials against DFT, then sample finer alloy concentrations and ternary configurations.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports quantitative agreement between one tested ML potential and DFT for both cohesion metrics, enabling expanded sampling including Ni56Fe20Cr24.
watch_item: Binary alloying trends do not quantitatively capture Fe–Cr interplay; explicit ternary calculations remain necessary.
paper_title: Alloying effects on the interface cohesion of grain boundaries in the Ni--Fe--Cr system
